newsitem.title: UK: UK harmonised CPI shows inflation at 2.2% y/y.
newsitem.headline: UK harmonised CPI shows inflation at 2.2% y/y.

text.p: British inflation, measured on a harmonised basis with European Union statistics, showed inflation of 2.2 percent in the year to January, the Office for National Statistics said on Wednesday.
The ONS said the figures do not replace Britain's retail price series but said it will supply the new data to Eurostat, the EU's official statistics organisation, on a monthly basis and publish them.
The harmonised figure is not as comprehensive as the RPI series, it said.
The harmonised figures have been constructed expressly for international comparisons and for assessing convergence as laid down by the Maastricht Treaty.

The new index differs from RPI in a number of respects. Owner occupiers housing and council tax are excluded from the new index, which is in the RPI. But it includes prices for new cars, computers and air fares not included in the RPI.
The new index uses a geometric rather than an arithmetic mean to aggregate the prices.
